name: Four-Week Running Calibration — Patched
description: Four-week daily running calibration bundle starting 2026-06-29. Patched to require Garmin chest-strap HR for calibration-quality data, remove Week 1 steady work, and add one optional diagnostic LTHR calibration test in Week 3. Weekly targets: Week 1: 46.5 mi, strap validation and easy-only baseline, 1 stride day, no steady/threshold, 1 long easy run; Week 2: 48.0 mi, small extension with first controlled aerobic check, 1 stride day, 1 easy-to-steady progression if strap data is clean, 1 long run; Week 3: 49.0 mi, highest calibration load plus optional diagnostic LTHR test, 1 stride day, 1 optional LTHR test or fallback steady audit, 1 long run; Week 4: 42.5 mi, deload, zone review, and next-block decision, reduced stride dose, short steady check only if fresh, reduced long run

card_templates.name: Recovery Run
card_templates.summary: Very easy run used to restore legs while preserving the daily running habit.

payload.talk_test: Full conversation; effort should feel almost too easy
payload.hr_guidance: During calibration, do not chase Garmin zones. Record them after. Use Garmin chest strap for calibration-quality HR; if using wrist HR, log the run as non-calibration-quality.

segments.label: Settle in
segments.detail: Start slower than instinct. Let breathing and cadence normalize.

segments.label: Recovery mileage
segments.detail: Keep the run soft, relaxed, and deliberately unambitious.

segments.label: Walk reset
segments.detail: Walk until breathing is calm before logging notes.

card_templates.name: Easy Aerobic Run
card_templates.summary: Default Zone-2-by-feel run for aerobic base and calibration.

payload.talk_test: Full sentences. You should not need mental toughness
payload.hr_guidance: Use RPE and talk test first. Garmin zones are audit data until calibrated. Use Garmin chest strap for calibration-quality HR; if using wrist HR, log the run as non-calibration-quality.

segments.label: Easy start
segments.detail: First mile slower than average pace. Do not correct upward.

segments.label: Aerobic cruise
segments.detail: Hold relaxed breathing and posture. Pace is secondary.

segments.label: Easy finish
segments.detail: Finish no harder than the middle of the run.

card_templates.name: Easy Run + Strides
card_templates.summary: Easy aerobic run with relaxed fast strides for mechanics, cadence, and leg pop.

payload.talk_test: Easy during the run; strides are too short to judge by talk test
payload.hr_guidance: Ignore HR during strides. Use full recovery and judge form. Use Garmin chest strap for calibration-quality HR; if using wrist HR, log the run as non-calibration-quality.

segments.label: Easy running
segments.detail: Run easy first. Do not let anticipation of strides raise the pace.

segments.label: Strides
segments.detail: Fast-relaxed, tall posture, quick feet. Walk/jog 60-90s between.

segments.label: Cooldown jog
segments.detail: Easy jog home. Calves should not feel cooked.

card_templates.name: Easy Run + Form Drills
card_templates.summary: Easy aerobic run followed by short mechanics drills for posture and coordination.

payload.talk_test: Easy run remains conversational; drills stay crisp
payload.hr_guidance: Drills are technique, not conditioning. Use Garmin chest strap for calibration-quality HR; if using wrist HR, log the run as non-calibration-quality.

segments.label: Easy run
segments.detail: Relaxed aerobic mileage.

segments.label: A-skips
segments.detail: Tall posture, quick ground contact, no stomping.

segments.label: High knees
segments.detail: Rhythm and posture over height.

segments.label: Butt kicks
segments.detail: Quick turnover; keep knees under hips.

segments.label: Straight-leg bounds
segments.detail: Light snap from the hips and ankles, not max power.

card_templates.name: Steady Aerobic Check
card_templates.summary: Controlled aerobic run for calibrating easy-versus-steady effort without threshold work.

payload.talk_test: Sentences possible. If you are reduced to phrases, back off
payload.hr_guidance: This is useful for mapping Garmin zones, but do not force HR into a prescribed zone. Use Garmin chest strap for calibration-quality HR; if using wrist HR, log the run as non-calibration-quality.

segments.label: Easy warmup
segments.detail: Ease into the run; do not start steady.

segments.label: Controlled steady block
segments.detail: Steady aerobic pressure, never threshold. Keep breathing controlled.

segments.label: Easy cooldown
segments.detail: Return to conversational running.

card_templates.name: Easy-to-Steady Progression
card_templates.summary: Easy run that finishes slightly steadier only when the body gives permission.

payload.talk_test: Full sentences early; controlled sentences near the end
payload.hr_guidance: Let HR be observed, not targeted. Use Garmin chest strap for calibration-quality HR; if using wrist HR, log the run as non-calibration-quality.

segments.label: Easy first half
segments.detail: Stay in true easy effort.

segments.label: Optional steady finish
segments.detail: Only drift to steady if legs and breathing are good. No tempo.

segments.label: Easy finish
segments.detail: Back off before stopping.

card_templates.name: Long Easy Run
card_templates.summary: Comfortable long run for aerobic durability and HR-drift calibration.

payload.talk_test: Full sentences for most of the run. Last 20 minutes may require focus but not strain
payload.hr_guidance: Use this to audit drift. Do not chase a faster finish during calibration. Use Garmin chest strap for calibration-quality HR; if using wrist HR, log the run as non-calibration-quality.

segments.label: Conservative start
segments.detail: Start slower than expected. First 20 min should feel trivial.

segments.label: Aerobic duration
segments.detail: Comfortable rhythm. Fuel/hydrate if needed.

segments.label: Controlled finish
segments.detail: Maintain form without pressing pace.

card_templates.name: Weekly Running Calibration Review
card_templates.summary: Weekly audit of RPE, Garmin zones, fatigue, and next-week adjustment signals.

payload.instructions: Use this after the final recovery run of each week. The goal is not judgment; the goal is better signal.

items.label: What pace range actually felt easy this week?
Where did Garmin zones disagree with talk test/RPE?
Any calf, Achilles, hamstring, knee, hip, or foot signals?
Heat, sleep, work stress, hydration notes?

card_templates.name: HR Strap Calibration Setup
card_templates.summary: Pre-run checklist to make HR data usable for zone calibration.

payload.instructions: Use this before the first run and repeat mentally before every calibration run. The point is not gadget obedience; the point is clean data.

items.label: Wear Garmin chest strap
items.detail: Wet the electrodes, tighten the strap enough that it does not slide, and pair it before starting the run.

items.label: Verify HR source
items.detail: Confirm the watch is reading from the strap, not wrist optical HR.

items.label: Watch for early spikes
items.detail: If HR jumps unrealistically in the first 5-10 minutes, reseat the strap and mark the run as partial calibration quality.

items.label: Log calibration quality
items.detail: After the run, record strap used yes/no, signal quality, RPE, talk test, and Garmin zone mismatch.

card_templates.name: Optional LTHR Calibration Test
card_templates.summary: One diagnostic lactate-threshold HR calibration test after 10-14 days of clean strap data.

payload.rpe: Progressive to hard-controlled; never all-out sprinting
payload.talk_test: Final 30-minute field-test portion should be short phrases only, but controlled enough to avoid blowing up
payload.hr_guidance: Chest strap required. Preferred option is Garmin guided Lactate Threshold Test if available. Fallback is the 30-minute field test below. Do not use wrist HR for this test.
payload.instructions: Readiness gate: At least 10 days of mostly clean chest-strap HR data; No calf/Achilles/hamstring/knee pain above mild background noise; No unusual fatigue, illness, poor sleep, or heat stress; Previous two easy runs felt genuinely easy by talk test Skip if: Strap signal has been unreliable; Legs feel flat or sore from lifting/running; Weather is unusually hot/humid; You feel tempted to race the test After the run, log: Test option used: Garmin guided / 30-min field test / skipped; HR source: Garmin chest strap required; Chest strap signal quality: clean / dropouts / spikes; If field test: average HR for final 20 minutes; If Garmin guided: detected LTHR and pace, if provided; Perceived control: did you blow up, negative split, or stay even?; Weather and surface; Recommendation: update zones now / wait for more data / retest later

segments.label: Warm-up
segments.detail: Easy running only. Finish with relaxed breathing and no leg heaviness.

segments.label: Primer strides
segments.detail: Relaxed fast strides with 60-90 sec easy jog/walk between. These prime mechanics, not fitness.

segments.label: Option A: Garmin guided LTHR test
segments.detail: If your watch supports the guided Lactate Threshold Test, use that and follow the watch prompts with the chest strap connected.

segments.label: Option B: 30-minute field test
segments.detail: Hard-controlled and even. Do not sprint the first 10 min. Average HR for final 20 min is the rough LTHR estimate.

segments.label: Cooldown
segments.detail: Easy jog/walk until breathing is normal. No extra mileage chase.

routine_specs.name: Four-Week Running Calibration — Patched
routine_specs.notes:
Patched version: Garmin chest strap required for calibration-quality HR; Week 1 is easy-only baseline; Week 3 includes one optional diagnostic LTHR test with easy fallback. Regular threshold training remains excluded.

Baseline source: running-last-7-days.md. Baseline week: 49.05 miles; Seven consecutive runs, mostly 6-7 miles, with a 9-mile long run. Zone caveat: User reports Garmin zones likely read too hard. This patched bundle treats Garmin HR zones as observation data only until chest-strap data and one optional LTHR test provide a better anchor. Training priority: Calibration and consistency, not performance improvement. HR calibration policy: Garmin chest heart-rate strap for every calibration-quality run. If the strap is not used, mark the run as useful mileage but non-calibration-quality HR data. Do not rewrite zones after one odd run. Review after 10-14 days of strap data, then use Garmin guided LTHR test or field-test result as the main anchor. Calibration phases: Week 1: Easy-only baseline, strap validation, HR drift and talk-test audit. Strides are allowed because they are neuromuscular and fully recovered.; Week 2: First controlled steady-aerobic exposure if strap data is clean and easy effort is stable.; Week 3: Optional diagnostic LTHR calibration test. This is a test, not the beginning of threshold training.; Week 4: Deload, review zone settings, and decide the next real training block..

Intensity definitions: RPE 1-2: Recovery. Nose breathing may be possible but not required. Full conversation. You should feel better after than before.; RPE 2-3: Easy aerobic. Full-sentence talk test. Breathing present but calm. You could continue a long time.; RPE 3-4: Steady aerobic. Sentences still possible, but not casual storytelling. No burning legs; no threshold chasing.; RPE 4-5: Upper aerobic audit only. Short sentences, controlled. During this calibration block, do not let this become a race.; 6+: Avoid sustained RPE 6+ in this block. Strides may briefly touch fast mechanics, but recover fully between them.; diagnostic_lthr_test: One controlled diagnostic test only, preferably Garmin guided LTHR. Alternative: 30 min hard-controlled field test, using average HR from the final 20 min as a rough LTHR estimate. This is not a weekly threshold workout.

Weekly targets: Week 1: 46.5 mi, strap validation and easy-only baseline, 1 stride day, no steady/threshold, 1 long easy run; Week 2: 48.0 mi, small extension with first controlled aerobic check, 1 stride day, 1 easy-to-steady progression if strap data is clean, 1 long run; Week 3: 49.0 mi, highest calibration load plus optional diagnostic LTHR test, 1 stride day, 1 optional LTHR test or fallback steady audit, 1 long run; Week 4: 42.5 mi, deload, zone review, and next-block decision, reduced stride dose, short steady check only if fresh, reduced long run

prescription_override_json.instructions: Do this before Day 1. The full block only works if HR source is consistent. Wrist-HR runs are still valid mileage but should not be used to set zones.

Keep it boring-easy. Full-sentence talk test. Log whether Garmin calls this Z3/Z4 despite easy breathing. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
Easy run first, then 6 strides on flat ground. Strides are neuromuscular, not a workout. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
Let pace float. If legs feel heavy, cap at 45 min. This is not hidden aerobic training. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
No steady block today. Keep it easy-only so Week 1 gives clean baseline data. Use the Garmin chest strap and compare HR to talk test after the run.
Easy run followed by short drills. Keep drills crisp, not tiring. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.

Comfortable long run. Ignore pace if heat/humidity is high. Finish with the sense you could keep going. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.

Shorter recovery run. Add weekly calibration notes after: easy pace, HR drift, soreness, sleep. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
Week 1 review. Separate mileage/fatigue notes from HR calibration notes. Only chest-strap runs count as calibration-quality HR data.
Repeat the baseline pattern. Try to make the first mile almost embarrassingly easy. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
Same stride dose as Week 1. If calves are tight, reduce to 4 strides. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
Nasal-ish breathing if natural, but do not force it. Let cadence and posture stay relaxed. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.

First 40 min easy, final 15-20 min steady aerobic only if breathing stays controlled. This is not a tempo. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
Smooth easy run, then 2 rounds of drills. Stop drills if coordination gets sloppy. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
Add only a small long-run extension. Watch HR drift and perceived effort over last 20 min. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
Keep this as a real recovery day even if you feel good. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
Week 2 review. Separate mileage/fatigue notes from HR calibration notes. Only chest-strap runs count as calibration-quality HR data.
No progression today. Use it to check whether Week 2 accumulated fatigue. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
8 shorter strides. Full walking/jog recovery. Speed should feel snappy, not anaerobic. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
If the stride day created calf/Achilles tightness, make this 5 miles instead. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.

This is the only true hard diagnostic effort in the block. Prefer Garmin guided Lactate Threshold Test if available. If not, use the 30-minute field test and estimate LTHR from average HR over the final 20 minutes. Skip and do easy aerobic mileage if readiness is not good.
If you completed the LTHR test yesterday, keep this very easy and skip drills if legs feel heavy. If you skipped the test, perform the normal easy + drills version. Use chest strap for HR audit.
Longest run of the block. Do not add fast finish unless legs feel unusually good. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
Shorter recovery day to absorb the bigger long run. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
Week 3 review. Separate mileage/fatigue notes from HR calibration notes. Only chest-strap runs count as calibration-quality HR data.
Reduce ambition. This week is consolidation and better signal quality. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
Reduced stride dose. Stop at 4 if legs do not pop. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
Very easy. This should improve freshness, not fitness. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
Only 10-15 min steady in the middle. If fatigue is present, make the whole run easy. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
One relaxed drill round only. Keep it clean. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
Shorter long run. Goal is finishing fresher than Week 3. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.

After the run, write the 4-week review: true easy effort, HR drift, legs, shoes, heat, sleep. Use the Garmin chest strap; if strap data is missing, keep the run but mark HR as non-calibration-quality.
Week 4 review. Separate mileage/fatigue notes from HR calibration notes. Only chest-strap runs count as calibration-quality HR data.
